title: Unauthorized firmware acceptance
scenario: An untrusted package is accepted during update.
mitigation: Verify authorized package signatures before installation.
requirement: Invalidly signed packages shall be rejected before installation.
test: Submit a deliberately invalid signature in a simulated update and confirm rejection.
assumption: Attacker can submit a package; signature verification failure would need evidence.

title: Firmware rollback
scenario: An older authorized but vulnerable package is installed.
requirement: Packages below the authorized minimum version shall be rejected.
test: Attempt a downgrade using a synthetic older package and verify rejection.
assumption: Attacker can deliver an old package; rollback policy is unspecified.

title: Signing key disclosure
scenario: An unauthorized actor obtains signing authority.
mitigation: Protect keys and restrict signing permissions.
requirement: Signing operations shall require an authorized identity and produce audit records.
test: Attempt signing with an unauthorized test identity and verify denial.
assumption: Key custody and access controls require clarification.

title: Update endpoint exhaustion
scenario: Excess requests consume update service resources.
mitigation: Bound request rates and resource consumption.
requirement: Update services shall enforce configured resource and request limits.
test: Use a bounded synthetic load in a simulator and check rejection and recovery.
assumption: Endpoint is reachable; capacity and operational impact are unknown.

title: Unauthorized diagnostic programming
scenario: A privileged diagnostic operation is accepted without authorization.
mitigation: Enforce diagnostic session and authorization checks.
requirement: Programming requests without authorization shall be rejected.
test: Send an unauthorized simulated programming request and verify rejection.
assumption: Diagnostic interface exists; authorization design requires review.
